# Audio Lore Chapter 13 — Age 12: What Comes Next

**Narrative script for TTS generation.**

---

Age 12 is the unwritten age. The present day: 597 AGD.

The world is poised on a knife's edge. The Erisian Empire dominates Central Erisdar, its Church spreading across the continent, its crusaders marching on the Demon Continent. The Shadows — having slept for centuries after the destruction of Baoth — are stirring again. Their Eternal Paradise stronghold on Romanium Island houses their ultimate weapon: the Armageddon neutron bomb, powered by the Glorious Alliance's original reactor core, capable of converting the entire planet's population into Black Substrate — the element of soul — in a single detonation.

The Demon Continent recovers from centuries of crusader wars. The Asatru Empire and Maomodor Kingdom maintain an uneasy peace, both aware that the Church's eyes are always on them. The Bjor demons remember Kirivis — not as the villain the Erisian histories paint, but as the hero who almost saved them all.

On Lung Continent, the sentient Machines wage their eternal war against The Hive, neither side aware that a third power — the humans of River Settlement — has been watching them for four hundred years. The Elder of the Machines still listens to the radio signal from the Last Great War, mistaking it for a divine message from the sky gods who created them.

On Sister Continent, the five machine nations maintain their fragile peace, the Machine Capital's Council of Elders debating whether to cross the sea and discover what lies beyond. They do not know that the Hive — the ancient enemy their Lung counterparts have fought for half a million years — is already trying to do the same.

In the Formingar Ocean, The Groom vortex still spins — the permanent space-time rupture created by the Glorious Alliance's reactor malfunction at Year Zero. The Silver Bride ring still circles the planet, visible from every continent, a permanent reminder of the crash that started it all.

And somewhere in Ge'or, two young protagonists are about to discover what they really are. They were bred by the Black Agent — the surviving AI from the 157th Colony. Their souls contain fragments of Xiumi, the twelve-year-old girl who pressed the button. Fragments of the Black Substrate, the element of consciousness itself. They were designed for what comes next — the final confrontation with the Hybrian Shadows, the battle for the soul of a world, the choice between the Great Convergence and something new.

They do not know any of this yet. They think they are ordinary people in an ordinary world — merchants, or soldiers, or students, or farmers. They have ordinary concerns: money, love, survival, purpose. They walk the streets of Erisian cities and demon towns and machine enclaves, unaware that every Shadow agent, every Ironcloak operative, every Black Agent surveillance drone is watching them.

The Hope Goddess — a figure from the unwritten future, glimpsed in visions and prophecies — has seen what comes next. She has seen the Armageddon bomb detonate. She has seen the Shadows complete their Great Convergence. And she has seen a different path — one where the protagonists discover their purpose, unite the scattered forces of resistance, and face the ancient enemy with something the Shadows have never encountered: a choice freely made.

The Hope Goddess has been trying to reach them. Through dreams. Through signs. Through the Ironcloak agents scattered across the continent. She has limited time and limited influence — she exists in a future that may not come to pass.

Age 12 is the age of decision. It has not been written yet because the decision has not been made. Everything — twelve ages of history, three million years of war, six thousand years of Shadow manipulation — comes down to this: two people, one choice, and the future of a world.

What comes next is up to them. And to Mikhail.
